q: Which of the following penalties imposed on a Railway employee is not a Minor penalty :

options.A: Withholding of promotion for a specified period
options.B: Withholding of increment for a specified period
options.C: Reduction to a lower stage in the time scale of pay for two year without cumulative effect
options.D: Reduction to a lower stage in the time scale of pay for two year with cumulative effect

e: Reduction to a lower stage in the time scale of pay for two years WITH cumulative effect — that is the penalty which is not minor. Under Rule 6 of the RS (D&A) Rules, the minor penalties include withholding of promotion, withholding of increments of pay for a specified period (clause iv), and reduction to a lower stage by one stage for a period not exceeding three years WITHOUT cumulative effect (clause iii-b). Reduction to a lower stage with cumulative effect falls under the major penalties (clause v).

q: Which of the following penalties can not be termed as major penalty :

options.C: Reduction to a lower stage in the time scale of pay for a specified period with cumulative effect
options.D: Reduction to a lower time scale of pay for a specified period with a bar to the promotion.

e: Censure — that is the right answer. Option (B) is correct: censure is the lightest minor penalty and can never be termed a major penalty. Removal from service, reduction to a lower stage with cumulative effect, and reduction to a lower time-scale with a bar to promotion are all major penalties carrying far graver consequences. This provision exists for a practical reason in day-to-day railway working; keeping that practical picture in mind makes the fact far easier to retain than memorising it in isolation.
